history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV's town 'Thanjavur' is WRONG - the temple is in GANGAIKONDA CHOLAPURAM town, Ariyalur district (~70 km northeast of Thanjavur). Built by Rajendra Chola I after his Gangetic campaign and completed in 1035 CE, it anchored his new imperial capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram (the capital from ~1025 to ~1279 CE), now a largely vanished city of which this temple is the great surviving monument. The defeated kings are said to have sent pots of Ganga water that were poured into the Cholagangam tank, giving the town and temple their names ('the city of the Chola who took the Ganga'). The 55-m (180-ft) nine-tiered vimana, with an unusual parabolic profile, was deliberately kept shorter than the Thanjavur Big Temple as a mark of respect to his father Rajaraja Chola I's work. UNESCO inscribed it as a World Heritage Site in 2004 together with the Thanjavur and Darasuram temples as the 'Great Living Chola Temples' (Thanjavur was inscribed in 1987); it is administered by the ASI as a protected monument. It is an active temple with four daily rituals and many yearly festivals. Coordinates are APPROXIMATE (district-level geocode match).

name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple
town: Gangaikonda Cholapuram (CSV town 'Thanjavur' is WRONG - the temple is in Gangaikonda Cholapuram town, Ariyalur district)
town_description: Gangaikonda Cholapuram is a town in Udayarpalayam taluk, Ariyalur district, the former imperial Chola capital founded by Rajendra Chola I after his Gangetic expedition. It lies on Highway 81 connecting Tiruchirappalli and Chidambaram, about 50 km from Chidambaram and roughly 70 km northeast of Thanjavur, in the Cauvery delta near the Kollidam river.

travel.road: On Highway 81 between Tiruchirappalli and Chidambaram; connected by Tamil Nadu bus services
